questions.scenario: A patient with a pruritic vulvar plaque undergoes biopsy. The section includes the surface epithelium and underlying tissue.
questions.lead_in: Which arrangement of the abnormal cells is visible in the biopsy?
questions.stem: Which arrangement of the abnormal cells is visible in the biopsy?
options: Large pale cells dispersed among epidermal keratinocytes
Thin epidermis over a band of superficial dermal sclerosis
Exophytic squamous papillae with koilocytic atypia
A circumscribed dermal nodule with complex papillary glands
Immature basaloid cells replacing the upper squamous layers
choice_rationales: The pale cells interrupt the usual darker keratinocyte population within the epidermis.
A thin epidermis and sclerotic dermis would favor lichen sclerosus. Here the striking abnormality is within the epithelium.
Condyloma has outward branching stromal cores and koilocytes. This surface lacks that exophytic architecture.
Papillary hidradenoma forms a separate dermal glandular nodule. The pale cells here lie among keratinocytes.
Classic vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia shows impaired squamous maturation with basaloid cells extending upward. Here the conspicuous cells are large and pale.
questions.explanation: Scan the purple epidermis beneath the surface. Large pale atypical cells are interspersed among darker keratinocytes.
visual_clues: The epidermis is the darker band along the top.
Several pale cells are larger than the adjacent keratinocytes.
questions.visual_target: Pale atypical cells in the epidermis
questions.tested_concept: Distribution of atypical cells in a vulvar biopsy
questions.ground_truth_basis: Supplied lecture page and visible evidence on the selected image.

questions.scenario: A patient with a pruritic vulvar plaque undergoes biopsy. The section includes the surface epithelium and underlying tissue.
questions.lead_in: Which diagnosis best accounts for the architecture and abnormal cells in this section?
questions.stem: Which diagnosis best accounts for the architecture and abnormal cells in this section?
options: Lichen sclerosus
Extramammary Paget disease
Condyloma acuminatum
Papillary hidradenoma
Classic vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia
choice_rationales: Expect epithelial thinning with superficial dermal sclerosis rather than this pale intraepidermal cell population.
Large pale malignant cells scattered within the vulvar epidermis are the pattern described for Paget disease.
Expect exophytic fibrovascular papillae covered by koilocytic squamous epithelium.
Expect a circumscribed dermal tumor with a complex papillary glandular pattern and no epidermal connection.
Expect atypical immature basaloid squamous cells and loss of maturation toward the surface, rather than scattered large pale cells.
questions.explanation: The large pale intraepidermal cells support extramammary Paget disease. The lecture describes its plaque as potentially eczema like and notes that cytoplasmic mucin staining can help confirm the diagnosis.
visual_clues: Use the level of the atypical cells and their pale cytoplasm together.
questions.visual_target: Abnormal pale population within the vulvar epidermis
questions.tested_concept: Diagnosis of a vulvar plaque from epidermal histology
questions.ground_truth_basis: Supplied lecture page and visible evidence on the selected image.

questions.scenario: An additional teaching image shows cytoplasmic staining in the vulvar biopsy setting.
questions.lead_in: Which interpretation accounts for the bright staining pattern?
questions.stem: Which interpretation accounts for the bright staining pattern?
options: Diffuse staining of dermal collagen
A continuous band of surface keratin staining
Pink secretion filling the lumens of a dermal nodule
Strong staining limited to vessels below the epidermis
Intracytoplasmic material in dispersed atypical epidermal cells
choice_rationales: The brightest foci lie above the dermal interface inside epithelial cells.
The visible positive foci are discrete cells at different heights in the epithelium.
No circumscribed glandular nodule contains these foci.
The vivid pink cells sit within the surface epithelium, above the visible vessels.
Several individual large epithelial cells contain vivid pink material.
questions.explanation: The vivid material is inside large cells dispersed among keratinocytes. R10 describes cytoplasmic mucin staining as a way to support the diagnosis in this setting.
visual_clues: Locate the pink material within individual cells rather than along the surface or in the dermis.
questions.visual_target: Bright cytoplasmic material in scattered large epidermal cells
questions.tested_concept: Cytoplasmic staining in a vulvar intraepithelial lesion

questions.scenario: An ovarian mass is excised. A representative histologic field is shown.
questions.lead_in: Which tissue pattern dominates the displayed field?
questions.stem: Which tissue pattern dominates the displayed field?
options: Primitive neuroepithelial tubules in immature tissue
Short fascicles of bland spindle cells
Round follicles filled with dense eosinophilic material
Mucin rich signet ring cells infiltrating ovarian stroma
Nests of large cells separated by lymphocyte rich septa
choice_rationales: Primitive neuroepithelium forms crowded cellular tubules. The conspicuous profiles here have expanses of dense pink luminal material.
Fibroma shows interweaving spindle cells. This field is dominated by rounded luminal profiles rather than fascicles.
The dense pink material is inside rounded epithelial lined follicles, consistent with thyroid colloid.
Signet ring morphology reflects intracellular mucin. The dense pink material in this field is in follicular lumens.
Dysgerminoma shows nests or sheets of tumor cells and lymphocytes in fibrous septa. Here the largest pink structures are filled lumens.
questions.explanation: The rounded spaces contain dense pink colloid. Their epithelial rims establish a thyroid follicular pattern.
visual_clues: Look for the thin cellular rims around the dense pink centers.
questions.visual_target: Rounded follicles containing dense colloid
questions.tested_concept: Differentiated tissue in an ovarian mass
questions.ground_truth_basis: Supplied lecture page and visible evidence on the selected image.

questions.scenario: An ovarian mass is excised. A representative histologic field is shown.
questions.lead_in: Which diagnosis best fits the dominant tissue pattern in this ovarian mass?
questions.stem: Which diagnosis best fits the dominant tissue pattern in this ovarian mass?
options: Immature teratoma
Ovarian fibroma
Krukenberg tumor
Struma ovarii
Dysgerminoma
choice_rationales: Primitive neuroepithelium or other immature tissue would support this diagnosis. The displayed field instead shows differentiated colloid filled follicles.
The short bland spindle cell fascicles described for fibroma do not account for these epithelial lined lumens.
Mucin rich signet ring cells are the clue to this metastasis. The prominent material here sits within follicles rather than within signet ring cells.
The ovarian mass contains the thyroid follicles and colloid characteristic of this monodermal teratoma.
Large primitive germ cells in sheets or nests with lymphocyte rich fibrous septa would favor dysgerminoma.
questions.explanation: The thyroid type follicles support struma ovarii in an ovarian mass. The lecture associates this specialized teratoma with hyperthyroidism.
visual_clues: Trace several epithelial rims. The pink material is luminal across multiple follicles.
questions.visual_target: Colloid filled follicles of thyroid type
questions.tested_concept: Diagnosis of an ovarian mass from differentiated tissue
questions.ground_truth_basis: Supplied lecture page and visible evidence on the selected image.

questions.scenario: A histologic section from an ovarian tumor is reviewed to classify the lesion.
questions.lead_in: Which structural arrangement is present near the center of the field?
questions.stem: Which structural arrangement is present near the center of the field?
options: A cluster of cells surrounding a small pool of eosinophilic secretion
A laminated calcific sphere between tumor cells
A primitive neuroepithelial tubule lined by crowded immature cells
A thyroid follicle with smooth luminal colloid
A vascular core wrapped by tumor cells and projecting into a space
choice_rationales: A Call–Exner body has a small central secretion. The red cells at the center here are in a vascular lumen.
A psammoma body is a laminated calcification. The center here has a vessel with red cells and an adjacent cellular cuff.
Primitive neuroepithelium forms tubules. The structure shown is a projection with a vessel running through its center.
A thyroid follicle encloses colloid. Here a vascular core and its surrounding tumor project into a clear space.
Red cells identify the central vessel. Tumor cells surround the vascular core within a larger space.
questions.explanation: The central vessel, surrounding tumor cells and outer space form a glomerulus like Schiller–Duval body.
visual_clues: Locate the cluster of red cells near the center.
Follow the rim of tumor around the vessel and the space outside that rim.
questions.visual_target: Glomeruloid projection with a central vessel
questions.tested_concept: Architecture of a Schiller–Duval body

questions.scenario: A histologic section from an ovarian tumor is reviewed to classify the lesion.
questions.lead_in: Which ovarian germ cell tumor is best supported by the central architecture?
questions.stem: Which ovarian germ cell tumor is best supported by the central architecture?
options: Yolk sac tumor
Dysgerminoma
Immature teratoma
Embryonal carcinoma
Struma ovarii
choice_rationales: The vessel centered Schiller–Duval body is the characteristic architecture described for yolk sac tumor.
Sheets or nests of large cells with lymphocyte rich septa would support dysgerminoma. The central structure instead has a vascular core wrapped by tumor.
Immature neuroepithelial tubules would favor immature teratoma. The visible central red cells identify a vascular core.
The lecture lists CD30 and OCT3/4 among the findings used to characterize embryonal carcinoma. The visible Schiller–Duval architecture points to yolk sac differentiation.
Colloid filled thyroid follicles would support struma ovarii. The pink red center here is an erythrocyte containing vessel.
questions.explanation: The Schiller–Duval body identifies yolk sac differentiation in this ovarian tumor. R12 also lists AFP and glypican 3 as positive stains for yolk sac tumor.
visual_clues: Distinguish the blood filled core from the outer space around the projection.
questions.visual_target: Vessel centered Schiller–Duval body
questions.tested_concept: Ovarian germ cell tumor diagnosis

questions.scenario: An additional teaching field illustrates a second growth pattern in this category of ovarian tumor.
questions.lead_in: Which additional architecture is present in this field?
questions.stem: Which additional architecture is present in this field?
options: A loose reticular network around irregular spaces
A single central vessel cuffed by tumor and surrounded by a cleft
Closely packed thyroid follicles with smooth pink colloid
Thick sheets of pale cells separated by lymphocyte rich septa
Crowded elongated tubules made of primitive neural cells
choice_rationales: Thin tumor strands form a loose irregular mesh.
That describes a Schiller–Duval body. The dominant pattern here is a diffuse network.
The irregular spaces lack the uniform colloid filled appearance of thyroid follicles.
That would favor dysgerminoma. The displayed strands are thin and irregular.
Immature teratoma shows densely cellular neural tubules instead of this loose mesh.
questions.explanation: The second field shows a loose reticular network of tumor around irregular spaces. The lecture describes several yolk sac tumor patterns, so a vessel centered structure need not appear in every field.
visual_clues: Trace the thin tumor strands around the irregular pale spaces.
questions.visual_target: Loose reticular network surrounding irregular spaces
questions.tested_concept: Reticular growth in an ovarian yolk sac tumor
questions.ground_truth_basis: Supplied lecture page and visible evidence on the selected image.

questions.scenario: Sections from two separate pregnancy specimens are shown side by side. Compare the villi and their trophoblastic coverings.
questions.lead_in: Which comparison best describes the two fields?
questions.stem: Which comparison best describes the two fields?
options: Left: mixed villous sizes with patchier rims. Right: broadly enlarged villi with prominent rims.
Left: broadly enlarged villi with prominent rims. Right: mixed villous sizes with patchier rims.
Both fields: broadly enlarged villi with prominent trophoblastic rims.
Both fields: mixed villous sizes with patchy trophoblastic rims.
Left: broad edema with inconspicuous rims. Right: mixed villous sizes with the thicker rims.
choice_rationales: The mixed size population is on the right. The conspicuous peripheral cuffs are on the left.
The left has expanded villi with conspicuous dark peripheral trophoblast. The right has enlarged pale villi alongside much smaller profiles.
This describes the left well. On the right, much smaller villi remain visible among the enlarged profiles.
The right fits the mixed pattern. On the left, pale expanded cores and prominent peripheral proliferation predominate.
The darkest and most conspicuous peripheral trophoblastic bands lie along the enlarged villi on the left.
questions.explanation: The left field shows marked villous edema with prominent peripheral proliferation. The right mixes markedly edematous villi and smaller villi, with less conspicuous trophoblastic proliferation overall.
visual_clues: Compare several villi rather than a single profile.
Dark cellular rims are more striking on the left.
questions.visual_target: Villous size and distribution of trophoblast in paired fields
questions.tested_concept: Comparing villous edema and trophoblastic proliferation

questions.scenario: Sections from two separate pregnancy specimens are shown side by side. Compare the villi and their trophoblastic coverings.
questions.lead_in: Which pair best matches the morphologic patterns shown?
questions.stem: Which pair best matches the morphologic patterns shown?
options: Left: partial mole. Right: complete mole.
Both specimens: complete mole.
Left: complete mole. Right: partial mole.
Both specimens: partial mole.
Left: nonmolar villous change. Right: partial mole.
choice_rationales: The right field has the mixed size pattern. The more striking peripheral trophoblast and generalized villous enlargement are on the left.
The left fits complete mole. The right has a mixture of markedly enlarged and much smaller villi, supporting the representative partial mole pattern.
Marked edema and prominent circumferential proliferation favor complete mole on the left. The mixed villous population favors partial mole on the right.
The right fits partial mole. The left shows broadly enlarged villi and more prominent trophoblastic rims.
The right fits partial mole. In the supplied left example, the combination of extensive villous edema and conspicuous trophoblastic rims favors complete mole.
questions.explanation: These representative fields favor complete mole on the left and partial mole on the right. R17 notes that overlapping villous changes occur in practice and that triploidy can help confirm partial mole.
visual_clues: The left field has more conspicuous peripheral proliferation.
The right field contains two readily distinguishable size populations.
questions.visual_target: Contrasting complete and partial mole patterns in separate specimens
questions.tested_concept: Morphologic classification of two molar patterns

questions.scenario: Two separate breast specimens are shown side by side. The fields show different patterns of tumor growth in breast tissue.
questions.lead_in: Which pair describes the way tumor cells grow in the two fields?
questions.stem: Which pair describes the way tumor cells grow in the two fields?
options: Left: thin files of separate tumor cells. Right: irregular tubules in reactive stroma.
Both fields: irregular tubules in reactive stroma.
Both fields: thin files of separate tumor cells.
Left: irregular tubules in reactive stroma. Right: thin files of separate tumor cells.
Left: tumor confined within a preexisting duct. Right: thin files of separate tumor cells.
choice_rationales: The irregular lumens are on the left. The thin rows of individually separated cells are on the right.
This fits the left. The right has rows of individual cells without comparable rounded tubules.
This fits the right. The left has multiple distinct gland lumens in the stroma.
The left has haphazard glands and reactive fibrous stroma. The right has thin, linear cords of noncohesive cells.
The right does show linear files. On the left, numerous haphazard glands sit in reactive stroma, rather than a proliferation confined within one duct.
questions.explanation: The left section shows irregular tubules in desmoplastic stroma. The right section shows single files of discohesive cells and little comparable stromal reaction.
visual_clues: Look for the pale lumens on the left.
Follow a row of dark nuclei between stromal fibers on the right.
questions.visual_target: Glandular tubules on the left and single files on the right
questions.tested_concept: Comparing gland formation and single file growth

Dense pale collagen directly beneath an attenuated surface
Perinuclear clearing with irregular enlarged nuclei
Complex epithelial glands with slitlike lumens
Uniform basaloid cells replacing the full thickness
choice_rationales: Paget cells form a separate atypical population. The clear spaces here center on squamous nuclei.
Lichen sclerosus changes the superficial dermis. The visible clue here lies inside the squamous cells.

Papillary hidradenoma has true glandular lumens. These pale spaces are intracellular.
This field retains differentiated superficial squamous cells with focal nuclear halos.
